recent_posts.title: Mainframe simulator: Gibson (upgraded)
recent_posts.summary: Gibson is an open-source mainframe simulator designed for learning z/OS, RACF, and ACF2, as well as practicing cybersecurity and penetration testing in a safe, controlled environment. A new version has been released, allowing testers and learners to explore mainframe concepts through interaction, scripting, and exploitation of realistic vulnerabilities. Resources include a homepage with download links, a tutorial video, and a related article about the project.

recent_posts.title: The KelpDAO Exploit Was Not a Bug — It Was a Broken Invariant
recent_posts.summary: A $292M exploit of KelpDAO in April 2026 is analyzed not as a traditional hack but as a formal invariant violation. The attacker exploited a 1-of-1 verifier configuration on a LayerZero bridge, forging a cross-chain message that was accepted as valid. This minted unbacked rsETH tokens used as collateral on Aave, propagating invalid state across DeFi. The core failure: verification was applied to constraints, not semantics — every check passed, yet the system was fundamentally broken. The post argues for formal modeling of cross-system invariants and introduces VSEL (Verifiable Semantic Execution Layer) as a proposed solution requiring proofs to validate semantic execution, not just constraint satisfaction.

recent_posts.title: Security Fails at the System Boundary, Not in the Primitive
recent_posts.summary: Security failures in real systems rarely stem from weak cryptographic primitives. The actual problem is the absence of formal system-level invariants, global state machines, and adversarial models that account for composition across services, networks, and operators. Even formally verified components can fail to compose into a secure system when there is no explicit definition of what the system must preserve end-to-end. This applies to ZK proofs with unmodeled state, PQC deployments with vulnerable key lifecycles, and distributed systems with unverified consistency assumptions. Security must be treated as an emergent property of a well-constrained system, not a collection of individually correct parts.

recent_posts.title: How to setup VS Code for PowerShell development in WSL
recent_posts.summary: A guide for configuring Visual Studio Code to work with PowerShell development inside Windows Subsystem for Linux. Covers the setup process for integrating VS Code with PowerShell running in a WSL environment.

recent_posts.title: When AI Becomes the Attack Surface
recent_posts.summary: AI and automation are fundamentally changing cybersecurity threats by enabling attackers to exploit software supply chains, trusted workflows, and AI-assisted development at unprecedented scale and speed. Traditional vulnerability-focused security models are proving inadequate against these evolved attack patterns, where persistence now targets trusted artifacts and pipelines rather than system access. The shift represents a fundamental change in the threat landscape for 2026, requiring security teams to rethink their defensive strategies beyond conventional approaches.

recent_posts.title: World's largest Internet Domain Database
recent_posts.summary: THC claims to maintain the world's largest internet domain database, offering reverse-DNS, subdomain, and CNAME lookup capabilities. The database is available for bulk download, and a CLI tool exists for querying the datasets.

recent_posts.title: Free e-book: Intro to Bash Scripting for Developers
recent_posts.summary: A free e-book resource available on GitHub that introduces Bash scripting fundamentals for developers. The book covers basic shell scripting concepts and is aimed at those looking to learn command-line automation and scripting skills.

recent_posts.title: Offensive Enumeration: Active Directory
recent_posts.summary: A technical guide demonstrating offensive enumeration techniques for Active Directory environments using PowerShell commands. Covers methods for discovering and extracting information about domain users, groups, computers, and organizational structure that security professionals and penetration testers use to assess network vulnerabilities.

recent_posts.title: Free Critical Risks scan (no signup)
recent_posts.summary: Pentester.com offers a free security scanning service that checks for critical risks associated with email addresses or website URLs without requiring signup. The scan completes in under 30 seconds and includes data from five dark web sources to identify potential security vulnerabilities and compromised credentials.

recent_posts.title: Unexpected exposures in SSH
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses a DEF CON video presentation that explores unexpected security issues in SSH and introduces 'sshamble', an open-source tool developed in Go for research and security testing of SSH services.
